title: Removing a Nested Contributor requires a SKY holder vote on top of the SPK vote for three years
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6.1 imposes a time-limited restriction: "For a period of three years after June 4, 2025, any Artifact Edit that would have the effect of removing a Nested Contributor must be approved by a vote of SKY holders in addition to a vote of SPK holders to be effective."

This is a double-key requirement, and note the phrasing — it catches any edit that "would have the effect of" removal, not only an edit that names removal as its purpose. That closes the obvious circumvention of achieving removal through a series of individually innocuous changes.

The protection is symmetric to the Nested Contributor's exemption from the proposal threshold. Contributors are given standing without capital; in exchange, their removal is not left to the Agent's own token holders, who could otherwise expropriate the value of work already contributed. Both provisions concern the same vulnerability: a party that is essential but not adequately shielded by ownership.

The three-year sunset marks this as scaffolding for the early period, when a young Agent depends heavily on a handful of teams. After it expires, SPK holders regain unilateral control — the protection is a bootstrapping measure, not a permanent feature of the relationship.
description: For three years from June 4, 2025, Spark's own token holders cannot unilaterally cut out a contributor that is also core to Sky — the parent ecosystem holds a veto.
